intro_html: Pozole is warm, hearty, and hominy makes it stick to your ribs in the best way. This one is built for meal prep, packing solid protein into a cheap-per-serving bowl with real depth of flavor. One batch makes 14 servings.
cost_closing_html: About $3.96 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Each of the 14 servings lands around 55g protein for about 549 calories, at roughly $2.50 a bowl.
upsell_html: This is the kind of bowl that feels like a hug after a long day, and it is waiting all week. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: Canned hominy is the cheap, filling base here, and it stretches the batch without stretching your budget.
The value pack chicken breast is your best friend for keeping the per serving cost down.
A little shredded cabbage on top adds crunch for pennies instead of pricier garnishes.
make_it: Place the chicken breast in the crock with the chopped onion.
Pour in both cans of enchilada sauce and a drizzle of olive oil.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 8 hours until the chicken shreds easily.
Shred the chicken, then stir in the drained hominy and let it heat through.
Shred the cabbage while the pot warms up.
Ladle into bowls and top each with a handful of crisp cabbage.

head.description: A high-protein Mexican meal prep. Fourteen servings at about 549 calories and 55 grams of protein for roughly $3.96 each (at everyday cost).
